summary.headline: GIPCL guides FY27 EBITDA to Rs950-1,000 crore at full run-rate, anchored by 600 MW Khavda solar at 33% CUF and Rs355 crore EBITDA.
summary.overview: Management held a post-Q4 FY26 conference call (dated 10 July 2026) covering the 600 MW Khavda solar asset, the 500 MW Khavda phase under evacuation constraints, and a planned 750 MW lignite expansion. Solar EBITDA was about Rs332 crore in FY26 and the company guided FY27 EBITDA to roughly Rs950-1,000 crore only once the 500 MW is fully operational. Interest and depreciation are set to roughly double, which compresses PBT in FY27-28. Management also flagged a 200 MW Khavda land-optimisation add and a BESS conversion at the Baroda gas site. Several answers were given as rough estimates and were not reconciled across questions.

financial_highlights.metric: FY26 RE revenue: solar ex-Khavda Rs152 crore, wind Rs86 crore, 75 MW solar Rs38 crore, Khavda 600 MW Rs111 crore
Expected FY27 company EBITDA at full run-rate (500 MW commissioned)
financial_highlights.change: Not in FY27 fully; management said it would appear in a full operational year
FY27 guided Rs350-450 crore (figures varied across answers)
Peak debt guided Rs4,500 crore, Rs6,000-6,500 crore including thermal
vs Rs13 crore previous quarter; includes Rs17 crore income tax refund

financial_highlights.metric: Capital work in progress (500 MW Khavda)

segments.name: Thermal (SLPP 1 and 2, lignite)
segments.commentary: FY26 revenue Rs1,103 crore; PLF above 75% at SLPP 1 and 80% at SLPP 2 per management. Thermal stations are described as debt-free.

segments.name: Solar - Khavda 600 MW
segments.commentary: Commissioned December 2025 with full CTUIL allocation from November 2025; CUF 33.24% in the current quarter versus about 23% in Q4 FY26 (teething phase). Management expects 30%+ annual CUF.

segments.name: Solar - Khavda 500 MW (phase 2)
segments.commentary: Advanced commissioning in phases of 200 MW, 200 MW and 100 MW, contingent on CTUIL evacuation readiness (post-monsoon, around end-2026). Rs2,065 crore CWIP sits against it.

segments.name: Solar - Raghanesda and other
segments.commentary: CUF about 28-29% at Raghanesda per management. Wind and 75 MW solar contributed Rs86 crore and Rs38 crore in FY26.

segments.name: Khavda solar park (park developer)
segments.commentary: Park allotted 2,375 MW; GIPCL builds 1,100 MW itself and has sold the rest to third parties (Coal India, SJVN, SAEL). Expected net park income Rs20-25 crore a year, O&M revenue Rs50-60 crore, for 25 years.

segments.name: Gas-based stations (Baroda, ~310 MW)
segments.commentary: Idle, with no revival expected given geopolitics. Plan is to convert the site to a 120 MW BESS (GUVNL approved, tender in place), with a further 160 MW planned. Management also said it intends to hive off the gas assets from the books in the next couple of years.

guidance_outlook: FY27 top-line addition of roughly Rs450 crore (Rs400-425 crore from 600 MW Khavda plus Rs30-40 crore from the RE park), per management.
FY27 EBITDA about Rs950-1,000 crore only at full operation of 500 MW; management said this would not appear fully in FY27.
FY27 interest guided Rs250-270 crore and depreciation Rs425-450 crore (rough; will vary with 500 MW commissioning). FY28 guided depreciation Rs550-600 crore and interest Rs400-450 crore.
Dividend commitment reiterated, with PBT dependent on 500 MW commissioning timing; FY27 PBT guided around Rs220 crore.

750 MW lignite expansion: capex about Rs6,000 crore (Rs4,800 crore debt at 80:20, Rs1,200 crore equity), phased from 2027 to 2032-33. Tender with BHEL under evaluation; order expected by end of FY27 or Q4.
BESS: Rs250-300 crore capex for 120 MW at Baroda, around one year to operational, indicative Rs6 per unit cost; 200 MW Khavda add at Rs800-1,000 crore project cost (timing dependent on land).
capex_capacity: 600 MW Khavda solar commissioned December 2025; 500 MW phase 2 in stages (200/200/100 MW), dependent on CTUIL evacuation line, targeted by end-2026.
Khavda PGCIL connectivity expected by end of July 2026 per management; installation possibly from August.
750 MW lignite expansion, approval in principle from GUVNL under Section 62 cost-plus; capex ~Rs6,000 crore phased 2027-2033.
Additional ~200 MW solar at Khavda using optimised land, targeted within a couple of months; 200-300 MW solar addition envisaged over the next couple of years.
Lignite fuel stated as available for 750 MW plus 500 MW for the full PPA life.
Pump storage: company is bidding for government allocation and identifying sites.
demand_pricing: Solar tariff referenced at Rs2.73/unit; PPAs with GUVNL with 25-year tenure; no curtailment on the 600 MW firm allocation.
Management said Gujarat demand exceeds supply and GIPCL is top of merit order, so it is not exposed to backing down; Khavda evacuation constraints are the exception.
PPAs carry benchmark CUFs; penalties apply to GUVNL below the benchmark. Management says tariffs embed a margin over the CUF.
Management said Khavda CUF would be 29-30%+ annually, Raghanesda 28-29%.

qa_highlights.question: What is the revenue, EBITDA and debt profile for the 600 MW Khavda asset?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 revenue about Rs420 crore at 33% CUF, EBITDA Rs350-360 crore. Debt repayment starts after the one-year moratorium ended June 2026, with step-up repayment over the following years.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 500 MW Khavda need more debt, and what is peak debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Long-term borrowing about Rs4,500 crore post 500 MW commissioning; with thermal expansion, peak debt Rs6,000-6,500 crore. Full disbursement pending against contractor milestones.

qa_highlights.question: Why is FY26 Q4 other income Rs42 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Mainly insurance claims settled in FY26 plus Rs17 crore income tax refund, plus government grant amortisation and O&M contractor liquidated damages.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company looking at BESS and pump storage?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes: 120 MW BESS at Baroda gas site under GUVNL approval, with 160 MW planned later; pump storage is in the race for government sites.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 750 MW lignite expansion need equity?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Rs4,800 crore would be 80:20 debt and Rs1,200 crore equity, funded via internal accruals over five years, promoter infusion, dilution or market raise; no firm plan yet.

qa_highlights.question: Will the 310 MW gas stations be revived or hived off?
qa_highlights.answer: Revival depends on gas prices and geopolitics. Management said the gas assets exist in the books but are technically idle, and hive-off is being considered over the next couple of years.

risks_watch: Khavda evacuation (CTUIL) dependency for the 500 MW phase; commissioning timing and teething losses could hit PBT.
FY27 numbers were given inconsistently across answers (depreciation Rs350-450 crore, interest Rs250-270 crore); the reconciliation is needed before modelling.
Debt rising from ~Rs3,250 crore to ~Rs4,500 crore and then Rs6,000-6,500 crore with thermal; floating 7.8% coupon exposure.
Monsoon-season CUF dip in Q2 FY27 and the two-to-three-month lag in publishing PLF data.
Equity funding for the Rs1,200 crore equity component of the lignite project is undecided.
Gas-based stations idle; hive-off decision and book-value impact pending.
summary.management_tone: Confident on operations and the Khavda ramp-up, but evasive and often approximate on numbers, frequently answering with rough ranges and promising follow-up. Caution is shown on evacuation timing, equity funding and gas-station revival.
key_quotes: Once the 500 MW Khavda gets commissioned for the full operational year, hopefully, next year, you will see these figures on the paper.
Revenue would be around INR55 crores to INR60 crores.
So, we are pushing power generated from 600 MW full. That is why our CUF is 33%.

growth.why: Guides FY27 EBITDA of Rs950-1,000 crore and ~Rs450 crore top-line addition, but only at full operation of the 500 MW Khavda phase (CTUIL-dependent, around end-2026), so much of it will not show in FY27; backing is capacity-based with partial specifics (capex, stages, CUF 33.24%) and no quarterly growth figures stated.
